text: If the angular velocity of earth's spin is increased such that the bodies at the equator start floating, the duration of the day would be approximately : [Take $g = 10 ms^{-2}$, the radius of earth, R = 6400 $\times$ $10^{3} m$, Take $π$ = 3.14]

solution.body:
For objects to float

mg = m$ω^{2}$R

$ω$ = angular velocity of earth.

R = Radius of earth

$ω=\sqrt{\frac{g}{R}}$ ..... (1)

Duration of day = T

text: An object of mass $m_{1}$ collides with another object of mass $m_{2}$, which is at rest. After the collision the objects move with equal speeds in opposite direction. The ratio of the masses $m_{2}$ : $m_{1}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Before collision

 
[IMG]
 

After collision,

 
[IMG]
 

Applying momentum conservation,

$m_{1}v_{1} = m_{2}v$ $-$ $m_{1}v ..... (1)$

The question does not state the type of collision, but every collision has $e\leq 1$. Here $e=\frac{v-(-v)}{v_{1}-0}=\frac{2v}{v_{1}}$ and (1) gives $v_{1}=\frac{(m_{2}-m_{1})v}{m_{1}}$, so $e=\frac{2m_{1}}{m_{2}-m_{1}}$. Hence $e\leq 1$ requires $m_{2}\geq 3m_{1}$.

Among the options only 3 : 1 satisfies this: 2 : 1 needs e = 2, 1 : 1 gives $v_{1} = 0$ and 1 : 2 gives $v_{1}<0$. The ratio 3 : 1 is the elastic case,

$\therefore$ e = 1

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{v-(-v)}{v_{1}-0}=1$

$\Rightarrow$ $v_{1} = 2v ..... (2)$

Put value of $v_{1}$ in equation (1),

$m_{1} (2v) = (m_{2}$ $-$ $m_{1})v$

$\Rightarrow$ $2m_{1} = m_{2}$ $-$ $m_{1}$

$\Rightarrow$ $3m_{1} = m_{2}$ $\Rightarrow$ $\frac{m_{2}}{m_{1}}=\frac{3}{1}$

text: In a series LCR circuit, the inductive reactance $(X_{L})$ is 10$\Omega$ and the capacitive reactance $(X_{C})$ is 4$\Omega$. The resistance (R) in the circuit is 6$\Omega$. The power factor of the circuit is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given :

$X_{C} = 4\Omega$

text: A particle of mass m moves in a circular orbit under the central potential field, $U(r)=-\frac{C}{r}$, where C is a positive constant. The correct radius $-$ velocity graph of the particle's motion is :

$\Rightarrow r$ $\propto$ $\frac{1}{v^{2}}$

$\therefore$ the graph between r & v will be hyperbolic.

text:
Three rays of light, namely red (R), green (G) and blue (B) are incident on the face PQ of a right angled prism PQR as shown in the figure.


[IMG]

The refractive indices of the material of the prism for red, green and blue wavelength are 1.27, 1.42 and 1.49 respectively. The colour of the ray(s) emerging out of the face PR is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In the figure the right angle is at Q and the legs PQ and QR are equal, so $\angle P=\angle R=45^{\circ }$.

The rays fall normally on PQ and pass into the prism undeviated. Since each ray is perpendicular to PQ, its angle of incidence on face PR equals the angle between PQ and PR, that is $45^{\circ }$.

A ray leaves through PR only if this angle is less than the critical angle $C$, where $\sin C=\dfrac{1}{μ}$:

$\sin 45^{\circ }<\dfrac{1}{μ}\Rightarrow μ<\sqrt{2}=1.414$

Red light ($μ=1.27$) satisfies this and refracts out through PR. Green ($μ=1.42$) and blue ($μ=1.49$) exceed 1.414, so they are totally internally reflected at PR.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Evening Shift

text:
The velocity $-$ displacement graph of a particle is shown in the figure.


[IMG]

The acceleration $-$ displacement graph of the same particle is represented by :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The slope of the given v versus x graph is $m=-\frac{v_{0}}{x_{0}}$ and intercept is $c = + v_{0}$. Hence, v varies with x as

$v=-\left (\frac{v_{0}}{x_{0}}\right )x+v_{0}$ ...... (1)

where $v_{0}$ and $x_{0}$ are constants of motion. Differentiating with respect to time t, we have

$\frac{dv}{dt}=-\left (\frac{v_{0}}{x_{0}}\right )\frac{dx}{dt}$

or $a=-\left (\frac{v_{0}}{x_{0}}\right )v$ ........ (2)
 
Using Eq. (1) in Eq. (2), we get

$a=-\left (\frac{v_{0}}{x_{0}}\right )\left (-\frac{v_{0}}{x_{0}}x+v_{0}\right )$

$a=\left (\frac{v_{0}}{x_{0}}\right )^{2}x-\frac{v_{0}^{2}}{x_{0}}$

Thus the graph of a versus x is a straight line having a positive slope = $\left (\frac{v_{0}}{x_{0}}\right )^{2}$ and negative intercept = $-\frac{v_{0}^{2}}{x_{0}}$. Hence the correct choice is (a).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Evening Shift

text: The time taken for the magnetic energy to reach 25% of its maximum value, when a solenoid of resistance R, inductance L is connected to a battery, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Magnetic energy, U = $\frac{1}{2}$LI${}_{0}^{2}$

Given : U = 25% of $U_{0}$.

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{2}LI^{2}=\frac{1}{4}\times \frac{1}{2}LI_{0}^{2}$

$\Rightarrow I^{2}=\frac{I_{0}^{2}}{4}\Rightarrow I=\frac{I_{0}}{2}$

$\therefore$ $I=I_{0}(1-e^{-t/τ})$

$\Rightarrow \frac{I_{0}}{2}=I_{0}(1-e^{-t/τ})$

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{2}=e^{-t/τ}$

$\Rightarrow e^{t/τ}=2$

$\Rightarrow t=τ\ln 2$

$\Rightarrow t=\frac{L}{R}\ln 2$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Evening Shift

text:
A solid cylinder of mass m is wrapped with an inextensible light string and, is placed on a rough inclined plane as shown in the figure. The frictional force acting between the cylinder and the inclined plane is :

[The coefficient of static friction, $μ_{s}$ is 0.4]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


For translational equilibrium,

T + f = mg sin60${}^{\circ }$ ..... (1)

For rotational equilibrium,

Torque about center of mass should be zero.

$\therefore$ $τ_{com}$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ f $\times$ R $-$ T $\times$ R = 0

$\Rightarrow$ f = T ..... (2)

Putting value of (2) in (1),

f + f = mg sin60${}^{\circ }$

$\Rightarrow$ f =  $\frac{mg\sin 60^{\circ }}{2}=\frac{\sqrt{3}mg}{4}$ = 0.433 mg

$\therefore$ cylinder need minimum 0.433 mg friction force to stay in equilibrium.

But here maximum friction force possible, 

$f_{\max } =$ $μ_{s}$N

= $μ_{s}$mg cos60${}^{\circ }$

= 0.4 mg $\times$ $\frac{1}{2}$

= 0.2 mg

As maximum possible friction force is less than 0.433 mg. so cylinder will not stay in equilibrium. It will slide on the surface. So friction will be kinetic friction.

$f_{k} =$ $μ_{k}$ N

=$μ_{k}$ mg cos60${}^{\circ }$

= 0.4 mg $\times$ $\frac{1}{2}$

= $\frac{mg}{5}$

text: Two wires of same length and thickness having specific resistances 6$\Omega$ cm and 3$\Omega$ cm respectively are connected in parallel. The effective resistivity is $ρ\Omega$ cm. The value of $ρ$, to the nearest integer, is $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let length of each wire is l and area A. When they are connected in parallel then their effective area 2A.

From formula we know,

$R_{eq}=\frac{R_{1}R_{2}}{R_{1}+R_{2}}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{ρl}{2A}=\frac{ρ_{1}\frac{l}{A}\times ρ_{2}\frac{l}{A}}{ρ_{1}\frac{l}{A}+ρ_{2}\frac{l}{A}}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{ρ}{2}=\frac{ρ_{1}\times ρ_{2}}{ρ_{1}+ρ_{2}}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{ρ}{2}=\frac{6\times 3}{6+3}=2$

$\Rightarrow ρ=4$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Evening Shift

text: A galaxy is moving away from the earth at a speed of 286 kms$^{-1}$. The shift in the wavelength of a redline at 630 nm is x $\times$ $10^{-10} m$. The value of x, to the nearest integer, is $____________$. [Take the value of speed of light c, as 3 $\times$ $10^{8} ms^{-1}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
From Doppler effect, we know

$λ^{'}=λ\left [1+\frac{v}{c}\right ]$

here, $v=286\times 10^{3}$ m/s

$c=3\times 10^{8}$ m/s

$\therefore$ $λ^{'}-λ=\frac{λv}{c}$

$=\frac{630\times 10^{-9}\times 286\times 10^{3}}{3\times 10^{8}}$

= 6 $\times$ $10^{-10} m$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Evening Shift

text:
Consider a water tank as shown in the figure. It's cross-sectional area is $0.4 m^{2}$. The tank has an opening B near the bottom whose cross-section area is $1 cm^{2}. A$ load of 24 kg is applied on the water at the top when the height of the water level is 40 cm above the bottom, the velocity of water coming out the opening B is $v ms^{-1}$.

The value of v, to the nearest integer, is $___________$. [Take value of g to be $10 ms^{-2}$]


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]
 
Force at point A,

$mg + p_{0}A = pA$

$\Rightarrow$ $p = p_{0} +$ $\frac{mg}{A}$

Given, area of $A = 0.4 m^{2} = 0.4$ $\times$ $10^{4} cm^{2}$ and area of $B = 1 cm^{2}$

applying continuity equation 

$AV_{1} = av$ [$V_{1} =$ velocity at point A]

$\Rightarrow$ $V_{1} =$ $\frac{a}{A}v$

As A >>> a so $\frac{a}{A}$ very small 

$\therefore$ $V_{1} <<< v$

So we can neglect $V_{1}$ by assuming $V_{1} = 0$

On applying Bernoulli's theorem at points A and B, 

$p_{0}+\frac{mg}{A}+\frac{ρV_{1}^{2}}{2}+ρgh=p_{0}+\frac{ρv^{2}}{2}+0$

$\Rightarrow p_{0}+\frac{mg}{A}+0+ρgh=p_{0}+\frac{ρv^{2}}{2}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{mg}{A}+ρgh=\frac{ρv^{2}}{2}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{24\times 10}{0.4}+1000\times 10\times 0.4=\frac{1000\times v^{2}}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ v $\simeq$ 3 m/s
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Evening Shift

text:
The radius of a sphere is measured to be (7.50 $\pm$ 0.85) cm. Suppose the percentage error in its volume is x. 

The value of x, to the nearest integer, is $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, radius of sphere = (7.50 $\pm$ 0.85) cm

$\therefore$ r = 7.50 and dr = 0.85

We know, volume of a sphere $v=\frac{4}{3}πr^{3}$

taking log both sides, we get

$\ln v=\ln \frac{4π}{3}+3\ln r$

Differentiating both sides,

$\frac{dv}{v}=0+3\frac{dr}{r}$

$\therefore$ Fractional error in volume $\frac{dv}{v}=3\frac{dr}{r}$

$\therefore$ % error in volume,

$\frac{dv}{v}\times 100=3\frac{dr}{r}\times 100$

$=3\times \frac{0.85}{7.50}\times 100$

= 34%
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Evening Shift

text:
An infinite number of point charges, each carrying 1 $μ$C charge, are placed along the y-axis at y = 1 m, 2 m, 4 m, 8 m ...............

The total force on a 1C point charge, placed at the origin, is x $\times$ $10^{3} N$.

The value of x, to the nearest integer, is $__________$. [Take $\frac{1}{4πε_{0}}=9\times 10^{9}$ $Nm^{2}/C^{2}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$F_{total}=\frac{kq_{1}q_{2}}{r_{1}^{2}}+\frac{kq_{1}q_{3}}{r_{2}^{2}}+\frac{kq_{1}q_{4}}{r_{3}^{2}}+.....$

$=9\times 10^{9}\times 10^{-6}\left [1+\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )^{2}+\left (\frac{1}{2^{2}}\right )^{2}+\left (\frac{1}{2^{3}}\right )^{2}+\left (\frac{1}{2^{\infty }}\right )^{2}\right ]$

$=9\times 10^{9}\times 10^{-6}\left [\frac{1}{1-\frac{1}{4}}\right ]$

$\because$ $\left [S_{\infty }=\frac{a}{1-r}\right ]$ for G.P.

$=9\times 10^{3}\times \frac{4}{3}$ = 12 $\times$ $10^{3} N$
